subject: Subprocessor roster & export-path matrix — clarifications for FinBridge pilot
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finbridge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Bose <anika.bose@finbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 16:12:00 +0100
Subject: Request: detailed subprocessor roster & export-paths for pilot

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — FinBridge is excited to move the pilot forward. Before we kick off work with our legal and security teams, could you share the full subprocessor roster (current and any planned additions in the next 90 days) along with a mapping of data export paths for EU-resident customer traffic? Our reviewers need to confirm:

- Which subprocessors will have access to raw request/response data containing customer PII
- Any subprocessors that transit or process data outside the EU (country-level where possible)
- KMS/HSM provider and key residency for encrypted at-rest stores
- Any planned short-lived temporary processors or edge partners used for burst capacity

If you can attach a spreadsheet and a simple network/dataflow diagram that shows where tokens/outputs may egress EU boundaries, that will speed our review. Ideally we'd get this by EOD Wednesday so our SOC/Legal sync on Thursday can proceed.

Appreciate it — let me know if you need an NDA/DPA pointer.

Best,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Security
FinBridge

---
Attachment: none
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 18:42:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: detailed subprocessor roster & export-paths for pilot

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Attached is our preliminary roster and an export-path matrix (marked v3/v2 respectively). High level answers inline below; see the attachments for the full vendor inventory and per-country notes.

Quick answers:
- Access to raw request/response PII: only our telemetry/observability and logging partners (listed in the roster) receive request metadata by default. We do not send raw customer prompt text to analytics partners unless explicitly configured by the customer.
- Subprocessors that may process outside EU: one edge telemetry partner (EdgeFlow) has a US-based transit path for short-term bursts — noted in the matrix.
- KMS/HSM: our primary KMS is KeyHarbor (keys stored in eu-west-1 KMS HSM cluster). We keep key material in-region for EU customers unless a customer opts into cross-region backup.
- Temporary processors: we list planned burst-capacity partners in the roster; any short-term additions are flagged and have an accelerated onboarding checklist.

Attachments included: subprocessor_roster_v3.xlsx, export_path_matrix_v2.pdf.

Can you confirm whether the SOC/Legal team prefers a separate DPA addendum for the EdgeFlow transit case or if contractual commitments + an addendum clause in the DPA will be sufficient? I'll loop Marissa and Karthik for technical/contract context.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: subprocessor_roster_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
Attachment: export_path_matrix_v2.pdf (diagram stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 02:15:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Request: detailed subprocessor roster & export-paths for pilot

Kim — quick technical notes after scanning the roster (adding for Liam's context):

1) EdgeFlow (temporary burst telemetry):
- Current config: fleet collectors in eu-west-1, but for overflow they can route telemetry to a US ingestion cluster (us-east-1) for 2–4 hour windows.
- Mitigations available: TLS in transit + field-level redaction; contractual prohibition on storing raw prompts; 30-day auto-log-rotation with defined retention in the DPA addendum.

2) KeyHarbor KMS:
- Keys are HSM-backed and provisioned in eu-west-1 by default. Backup copies to eu-central-1 only. Cross-region backup to us-east-1 is opt-in and requires customer approval.
- We have the KMS provider's certificate summary attached (kms_provider_certificate_summary.pdf).

3) Observability stack (LogLens):
- Only alerting metadata is shipped by default; raw payloads masked. We should call out the masking rules in the matrix explicitly (I added a short column in the spreadsheet).

4) Suggested ask for FinBridge:
- If they have a strict data residency requirement (no EU->US transit under any condition), propose an EdgeFlow onshore fallback: route overflow to a on-prem / dedicated pool (Redwood Dedicated) located in eu-central-1. This is feasible but requires a short SLA/commitment change.

Kim — I can draft a short DPA addendum clause for the EdgeFlow transit exception if that helps. LMK.

—Marissa
Product Security
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: kms_provider_certificate_summary.pdf (certificate stub)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finbridge.com>, Anika Bose <anika.bose@finbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: detailed subprocessor roster & export-paths for pilot

Hi Liam / Anika — following up with the consolidated packet and next steps.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v3.xlsx, export_path_matrix_v2.pdf, kms_provider_certificate_summary.pdf

Summary / clarifications:
- Raw prompt text: by default, Redwood does not send raw prompt/response text to analytics or telemetry processors. The exceptions are temporary overflow windows where a short-lived ingestion path (EdgeFlow) may transit anonymized or redacted telemetry; we have called out exact fields in the matrix.
- EdgeFlow transit: the transit path to us-east-1 only occurs during overflow bursts (2–4 hour windows). We can: 1) add a DPA addendum clause requiring no persistent storage of raw prompts by EdgeFlow; 2) enforce field-level masking before any transit; or 3) route burst overflow to a Reserved Dedicated pool in eu-central-1 (requires commitment). Please indicate which remedy FinBridge prefers and we'll surface the appropriate contractual language.
- KMS/HSM: keys for EU customers are HSM-backed in eu-west-1. Cross-region backup to us-east-1 is strictly opt-in.

Next steps:
1) Let us know FinBridge's residency tolerance (zero EU->US transit vs allow transit with contractual mitigation).
2) If needed, we'll prepare a short DPA addendum (Marissa offered to draft).
3) Once we have preference, we'll update the roster matrix and provide a single-page summary for your SOC team.

Links: HubSpot company record (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/FinBridge) and our internal ticket SUP-2345 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-2345) for tracking.

Thanks — aiming to get the addendum language ready by Thursday if we have their preference.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
